newsitem.title: CANADA: Stronger employment to push housing starts up - CMHC.
newsitem.headline: Stronger employment to push housing starts up - CMHC.

text.p: Total Canadian housing starts will rise through 1997 and 1998, boosted by low mortgage rates, strong job creation and improving consumer confidence, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Friday.
The CMHC forecast total housing starts to rise to 141,800 this year and 150,700 in 1998. Single-detached starts will rise 14.5 percent in 1997 to 89,300 units.
In what would be the first significant increase in four years, multiple unit housing starts were forecast to rise 12.2 percent to 52,400 in 1997.

"Over the next two years, further momentum in housing will come from stronger private sector job creation, as consumer spending finally joins exports in boosting employment levels to new highs," Michel Laurence, senior economist at the CMHC market analysis center, said in a statement.
